items.stem: A student spends an hour studying economics instead of working a job that pays $15. The opportunity cost of that hour of studying is best described as:

options.text: The $15 of forgone wages (the value of the next-best alternative)
options.rationale: Correct: opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative given up.
Studying has an opportunity cost equal to what was given up.

options.text: The total of all possible alternatives combined
options.rationale: Opportunity cost is the single next-best alternative, not the sum of all.

options.text: The money spent on tuition that semester
options.rationale: Sunk tuition is not the forgone alternative for this hour.

items.explanation: Correct: opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative given up.

items.stem: Gross domestic product (GDP) is best defined as the market value of:

options.text: All final goods and services produced within a country in a period
options.rationale: Correct: GDP counts final output produced domestically in a period.

options.text: All goods ever produced in the country's history
options.rationale: GDP measures a single period, not cumulative history.
GDP includes domestic production, not only exports.

options.text: Intermediate goods counted at every stage
options.rationale: Counting intermediate goods would double-count; GDP uses final goods.

items.explanation: Correct: GDP counts final output produced domestically in a period.

items.stem: Which TWO actions are expansionary fiscal policy?

options.rationale: Correct: higher government spending raises aggregate demand.

options.text: Cutting taxes to raise disposable income
options.rationale: Correct: lower taxes raise spending and aggregate demand.

options.text: Raising the central bank's policy interest rate
options.rationale: That is contractionary monetary policy, not fiscal policy.

options.text: Reducing government spending to balance the budget
options.rationale: Cutting spending is contractionary fiscal policy.

options.text: Selling government bonds through open-market operations
options.rationale: That is a monetary-policy tool, not fiscal policy.

items.explanation: Correct keys: A, B. Correct: higher government spending raises aggregate demand. Correct: lower taxes raise spending and aggregate demand.
